assets.name: lecture_08_frame_01.png
assets.rationale: The localized-state sketch supports the opening TikZ reconstruction, but the lecturer obscures the barrier and wavefunction enough that the frame should not be printed.
assets.caption_hint: A left-localized trial state in a high-barrier double well.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Then this wave function would have a slightly lower energy.

assets.name: lecture_08_frame_02.png
assets.rationale: The symmetric continuation, central barrier, tunneling tail, and energy reference are visible together during the matching explanation.
assets.caption_hint: The symmetric wavefunction extending through a high central barrier.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The true ground state, the true energy eigenstate is this combination here.

assets.name: lecture_08_frame_03.png
assets.rationale: The center of the board is washed out, the level splitting is not legible, and the lecturer covers part of the drawing. The clean TikZ energy-level reconstruction carries the reliable content.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: When the two wave functions mix, the energy is lowered for the symmetric state.

assets.name: lecture_08_frame_04.png
assets.rationale: The upper combination and lower-energy label are visible, but the lecturer hides the denominator and the lower combination is incomplete. The equations are typeset from the transcript and board sequence.
assets.caption_hint: The symmetric and antisymmetric combinations while still being written.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Then we have psi left minus psi right over square root of two.

assets.name: lecture_08_frame_05.png
assets.rationale: The opposite relative phases and the condition e^(2 i epsilon t) = -1 are complete and unobstructed. The typeset derivation regularizes the sign convention explicitly.
assets.caption_hint: The relative-phase condition for complete transfer from the left well to the right well.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Minus one is e to the i pi, right?

assets.name: lecture_08_frame_06.png
assets.rationale: The paired magnetic-axis and charge-displacement sketches remain visible during the time-reversal conclusion. A TikZ reconstruction supplies the transformation logic that the live board leaves implicit.
assets.caption_hint: Magnetic moment and electric displacement before and after time reversal.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: You would find out that if time reversal symmetry were a good symmetry, you could not have the electron having a dipole moment.

assets.name: lecture_08_frame_07.png
assets.rationale: Both directions of the one-particle Fourier transform are complete, centered, and unobstructed immediately before the transition to field operators.
assets.caption_hint: Position- and momentum-space wavefunctions as a Fourier-transform pair.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: That's Fourier's theorem relating functions and their Fourier transforms.

assets.name: lecture_08_frame_08.png
assets.rationale: The mode commutator and local field commutator are visible together as the lecture explains how delta_ij becomes delta(x-y).
assets.caption_hint: Bosonic mode and equal-time position-space commutators.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It's just delta of x minus y.
